name: effects-css-import-webfont
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS, then hand-edited to add a Google Fonts @import and a url() texture
story: The type looked wrong in a browser, so the designer pasted a Google Fonts @import into the exported file's <style> block and a remote texture url() into the panel's fill rule.
idioms: @import url(https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bebas+Neue&display=swap); as the FIRST line inside <style>, unquoted and carrying a query string whose ampersand had to be XML-escaped to keep the document well-formed (the unescaped paste is its own fixture, geometry-unescaped-ampersand)
url("https://cdn.example.com/noise.png") inside a declaration block rather than on an attribute - a network reach with no href anywhere in the document
a quoted family with a real space in it (font-family:'Bebas Neue') rather than a PostScript face name, because it was pasted from the Google Fonts page

the ordinary Illustrator Internal CSS shell around it: Generator comment, version="1.1" id="Layer_1" x="0px" y="0px", style="enable-background:new 0 0 1920 1080;", xml:space="preserve", Responsive export so viewBox and no width/height
<style type="text/css"> as a direct child of <svg>, tab-indented .stN classes with one property each, several stacked on one element (class="st2 st3 st4 st5")
unitless letter-spacing:6 in its own class
growthNote: Written as grow-x when this fixture was drafted, and corrected before it was ever pinned. The panel behind the headline IS the full 1920x1080 frame, and §4 says a growing panel widens to the right and "stops inside the frame's safe margin" - a rectangle already drawn to the frame's own edges has no room to grow into, so growth is structurally impossible here whatever the ladder proposes. Shrinking is the honest remaining rung. The correction is argued from §4 rather than from the measurement, which is the rule this corpus is built on.
whyThisMatters: Every other file in the corpus reaches the internet through an href, which is the easy half. This one reaches it from inside a CSS declaration block, where no attribute scan can see it - and an exported graphic that fetches a stylesheet on air is exactly the failure the offline promise in root AGENTS.md non-negotiable 3 exists to prevent, because it fails only on the playout machine and only when the network is down. The @import is also the shape that would silently keep working in the studio preview, which is the worst way for it to survive. Pasting a webfont import is what a designer does when type looks wrong, so this is a habit rather than an accident.
